lease:
APARTMENT LEASE
Sunbelt Gardens - Building C

Landlord: Sunbelt Gardens Partners, Ltd.
Resident: Marcus Oyelaran
Unit: C-108, Sunbelt Gardens, 1270 Kestrel Way, Orlando, FL 32807 (an apartment in a 140-unit complex)
Lease Term: 12 months, from August 1, 2026 through July 31, 2027
Monthly Rent: $1,540.00, due on the 1st

ARTICLE 1 - DEPOSIT
1.1 Resident shall pay a security deposit of $1,540.00 at signing.
1.2 Landlord may deposit the security deposit in its general operating account and may use those funds for property expenses during the Lease Term.
1.3 Landlord will refund the deposit, less any lawful deductions, within 30 days after Resident vacates if no claim is made.
1.4 If Landlord intends to claim any part of the deposit, Landlord will notify Resident in writing within 45 days after Resident vacates.

ARTICLE 2 - RENT AND DEFAULT
2.1 A late fee of $100.00 applies to any rent received after the 3rd of the month.
2.2 If rent remains unpaid, Landlord may terminate this Lease after giving Resident a 3-day written notice; the 3 days are calendar days and include Saturdays, Sundays, and holidays.
2.3 If rent is more than 10 days late, Landlord may change the locks to the Unit until all amounts owed are paid in full.

ARTICLE 3 - UTILITIES
3.1 Resident is responsible for electricity and internet service.
3.2 Water and sewer are furnished by Landlord through a master meter and billed back to Resident monthly.
3.3 Landlord may shut off water service to the Unit if Resident's account is more than 15 days past due.

ARTICLE 4 - ACCESS
4.1 Landlord will give Resident at least 24 hours' notice before entering to make repairs, and will enter for repairs only between 9:00 a.m. and 5:00 p.m., except in an emergency.

ARTICLE 5 - MAINTENANCE
5.1 Landlord will maintain the roof, structure, plumbing, and common areas and will comply with applicable housing codes.
5.2 Resident will promptly report leaks and will pay for repairs to damage Resident or Resident's guests cause.

ARTICLE 6 - RENEWAL
6.1 Either party may end this Lease at the end of the term by giving written notice at least 30 days before July 31, 2027.

ARTICLE 7 - NOTICES
7.1 Notices to Landlord shall be sent to Sunbelt Gardens Partners, Ltd., 1270 Kestrel Way, Office 1, Orlando, FL 32807.

ARTICLE 8 - FEES
8.1 In any action arising from this Lease, the prevailing party shall be entitled to reasonable attorney fees.

Signed: ____________________ (Landlord)   ____________________ (Resident)

findings.title: How the security deposit is held
findings.problem: The lease lets the landlord mix the deposit with their own funds or use it before it is due. Florida requires a separate account in a Florida bank, or a surety bond.

span.quote: Landlord may deposit the security deposit in its general operating account and may use those funds for property expenses during the Lease Term.

findings.suggestedFix: Landlord will hold the security deposit in a separate non-interest-bearing account at a Florida financial institution and will not commingle it with other funds.

findings.title: Security deposit disclosure
findings.problem: The lease takes a deposit but doesn't include the required deposit disclosure. This can also be given in a separate written notice within 30 days, and doesn't apply to landlords with fewer than five units.

findings.title: Deposit return deadline
findings.problem: The lease gives the landlord 30 days to return the deposit when there is no claim. Florida requires 15 days or less, so this term is void.

span.quote: Landlord will refund the deposit, less any lawful deductions, within 30 days after Resident vacates if no claim is made.

findings.suggestedFix: Landlord will return the deposit when there is no claim within 15 days after the termination of the rental agreement.

findings.title: Deposit claim notice deadline
findings.problem: The lease gives the landlord 45 days to send written notice of a claim on the deposit. Florida requires 30 days or less, so this term is void.

span.quote: If Landlord intends to claim any part of the deposit, Landlord will notify Resident in writing within 45 days after Resident vacates.

findings.suggestedFix: Landlord will send written notice of a claim on the deposit within 30 days after the termination of the rental agreement.

findings.title: Notice for unpaid rent
findings.problem: The lease counts weekends or holidays in the unpaid-rent notice period. Florida excludes Saturdays, Sundays and court-observed holidays.

span.quote: If rent remains unpaid, Landlord may terminate this Lease after giving Resident a 3-day written notice; the 3 days are calendar days and include Saturdays, Sundays, and holidays.

findings.suggestedFix: If rent is unpaid, Landlord may terminate this lease only after delivering a written 3-day notice; the 3 days exclude Saturday, Sunday, and court-observed legal holidays.

findings.title: Utility shutoff
findings.problem: The lease allows the landlord to shut off or interrupt utilities. Florida prohibits this, even when rent is late.

span.quote: Landlord may shut off water service to the Unit if Resident's account is more than 15 days past due.

findings.suggestedFix: Delete the clause. Landlord will not interrupt any utility service furnished to Tenant.

findings.title: Lockout
findings.problem: The lease allows the landlord to change the locks or otherwise keep the tenant out. Florida prohibits self-help lockouts; only a court eviction can remove a tenant.

span.quote: If rent is more than 10 days late, Landlord may change the locks to the Unit until all amounts owed are paid in full.

findings.suggestedFix: Delete the clause. Landlord may recover possession only through a court eviction.
